nodes.label: Next.js Breaking-Changes Notice
nodes.rationale: Trained Next.js knowledge may be stale for this project because it intentionally deviates from conventional Next.js APIs/conventions/file structure; code must be verified against node_modules/next/dist/docs before writing, to avoid using deprecated or nonexistent APIs from training data.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Graph outputs must remain trustworthy: never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS instead), never skip the corpus-size warning, always show token cost, never hide cohesion scores behind symbols, and never silently render an oversized HTML viz - trust depends on visible uncertainty (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS) rather than hidden confidence.

nodes.label: Node ID Format Rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must be {full-repo-relative-path-with-every-segment}_{entity}, matching exactly what the AST extractor generates, so semantic-extraction nodes and AST nodes for the same symbol collapse into one node instead of creating duplicate 'ghost' orphan nodes; using just the filename or only the immediate parent directory breaks this collision and fragments the graph.

nodes.label: Confidence Score Rubric
nodes.rationale: A continuous 0-1 confidence range is empirically collapsed by models into a bimodal distribution (>50% at the 0.5 default, >40% at 0.85+); replacing it with a fixed discrete rubric of five specific values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) makes models follow the intended range more faithfully than free-form continuous scoring, with anything below routed to AMBIGUOUS instead of a low float.

nodes.label: Constrained Query Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify's query CLI (and its inline fallback) matches nodes via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, no synonyms, and no cross-language matching; a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's node-label vocabulary silently collapses the answer to zero hits. Expanding the query against the graph's own extracted label vocabulary before traversal - selecting only tokens that actually exist in that vocabulary, never inventing new ones - fixes the mismatch without hallucinating false matches.

nodes.label: Whisper Domain-hint Prompt
nodes.rationale: Rather than making a separate LLM API call to produce a Whisper initial-prompt, the host agent - already an LLM - composes a one-sentence domain hint directly from the corpus's existing god-node labels (or a generic fallback for video-only corpora), saving a redundant call while still steering transcription accuracy toward the corpus's actual vocabulary.
